finding.claim: The avatar endpoint fetches a user-supplied URL server-side. The only check is that the string starts with "https://". Nothing restricts the host, so an attacker can target internal HTTPS services, hostnames that resolve to private or link-local IPs (for example users.internal or a DNS-rebinding domain), and cloud metadata endpoints reachable over HTTPS. axios follows redirects by default, so an attacker's HTTPS server can 302 to http://169.254.169.254/ or http://users.internal:8080/ and bypass the https-only check. The response is not returned, but the byte length is. This gives an oracle for reachability and response size (blind or semi-blind SSRF).

trace.note: Only check: typeof string and startsWith("https://")
axios.get(url) with default redirect following (maxRedirects 5), no host or IP allowlist
Response size is returned to the caller, leaking reachability and size of internal resources

finding.guards_checked: Scheme prefix check (https only). This does not stop internal hosts, private or link-local IPs, DNS rebinding, or redirects to http:// targets. No host allowlist, no IP-range blocklist, no maxRedirects:0 or redirect validation, and no auth middleware. The second route (GET /users/:id, server.js:18-21) was checked and is not reported. The host is a fixed constant, and encodeURIComponent stops the attacker from injecting slashes, a host or a query string. The value is still a single path segment, so a bare ".." could shift the path by one level within the same internal service. That is path manipulation rather than SSRF to an arbitrary host.

verdict.guard_found: Only a scheme prefix check (typeof string and startsWith("https://")) at server.js:11; no host allowlist, no IP blocklist, no maxRedirects restriction, no auth middleware.
verdict.reason: server.js:10 takes req.body.avatarUrl from an unauthenticated route, and server.js:14 passes it to axios.get after only the scheme-prefix check at server.js:11. axios follows redirects by default, and server.js:15 returns the response byte length, so this is a semi-blind SSRF.
